question: True or false: for over 30 years, the first side of Kind of Blue sounded higher than the band played?
answer: True. A tape machine at the 1959 session ran slow, so the master played back fast and a little sharp, well under a semitone, on So What, Freddie Freeloader and Blue in Green. An engineer caught the error only in 1992. Players transcribing those solos had found the band tuned somewhere between keys.
move: The most copied version is not always the version that happened.
ask: Which version of something I know best is the copy and not what actually happened?
trap: Assuming the best-selling jazz album was checked note for note.
reference: Kahn, Kind of Blue: The Making of the Miles Davis Masterpiece, Da Capo Press, 2000
